chapter: Jelly Roll Morton and Oliver anecdotes
title: Touring with Jelly Roll Morton's band
summary: Moore worked about two months with Morton, playing one-nighters in Pennsylvania in cars that broke down, costing a job's pay.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Remembering Jelly Roll Morton: the man, the band

blocks.x: You could use wood blocks. Yeah, your wood blocks. And your car bell. You work with Jelly too? Well, I've done something with Jelly, Jelly at old Martin. How about? Oh, about two months. He had his, had about four or five automobiles, Cadillacs. Lincoln. Lincoln, yeah. So he diamonds? Yeah. He's playing all through Redding, Pennsylvania, and Philadelphia. Next time. Yeah. That's great. Yeah. He's playing them one night stands, you know. Sometimes the cars, one or two of the cars would break down. One or two of the jobs we didn't make. Car broke down. Some of the fellas got there, waiting on us, on the drummer. The car was in. Broke down. The drummer wasn't there. So when we did get there, we supposed to start at 9 o'clock. From 9 to 1. When we did get there, we got there at 11 o'clock. Everybody done demand the money back. We didn't get paid for that job. Jelly at old was a good fellow. He was a great piano player. If he hadn't had a, had a bus, he started those cars. A little up-to-date bus, he started those cars. But his car was kind of old, I don't know how he was. 38, 39. Yeah, probably.
